description: Redevelopment to provide a three storey building with a convenience retail store (Class E) at ground level and six residential units (Class C3) at first and second floor with associated servicing bay, vehicle crossover to the High Street, car and cycle parking, amenity areas and landscaping following demolition of the existing buildings
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92 (1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [WP-0795-A-0002 Revision P1, WP-0795-A-0010 Revision P1, WP- 0795-A-0011 Revision P1, WP-0795-A-0020 Revision P1, WP-0795-A-0021 Revision P1, WP-0795-A-0030 Revision P1, Design & Construction Method Statement, Design and Access Statement Revision P1, Daylight and Sunlight Assessment, Cover Letter, Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment, Arboricultural Statement, Ecological Impact Assessment, Evacuation Lift Management, Fire Statement, Framework Residential Travel Plan, Framework Workplace Travel Plan, Heritage Statement and Archaeological Assessment, Landscape Management Plan, Transport Statement, Statement of Community Involvement, Sequential Assessment, Planning Statement, Phase 1 Contaminated Land Assessment - Volume 1, Phase 1 Contaminated Land Assessment - Volume 2, Noise Impact Assessment Revision B and Lighting Impact Assessment Revision A. Received on 24/07/2023; Road Safety Audit Stage 1. Received on 09/08/2023; Design and Access Statement Addendum, Cover Letter and P20-0405_EN_002_C_0001. Received on 31/10/2023; Addendum to Noise Impact Assessment. Received on 13/11/2023; Daylight and Sunlight Assessment Addendum and Transport Statement Addendum. Received 22/12/2023; WP-0795-A-0001 Revision P2, WP-0795-A-0101 Revision P4, WP-0795-A-0102 Revision P4, WP-0795-A-0103 Revision P4, WP-0795-A-0200 Revision P5, WP-0795-A-0105 Revision P5, WP-0795-A-0104 Revision P5, WP-0795-A-0100 Revision P5, WP-0795-A-0201 Revision P5, Air Quality Assessment Revision C, Biodiversity Metric Calculation, Energy & Sustainability Statement Revision E and Overheating Assessment Revision B. Received on 19/02/2024; P20-0405_EN_001_E_0001, P20-0405_EN_001_G_0002 and Surface Water Drainage Strategy Revision D. Received on 21/02/2024].

Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 5 - The ground floor commercial premises of the development hereby permitted shall not be used for any purposes other than as retail (Use Class E(a)), and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Use Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or in any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification).

Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining premises but would wish to control the operations of the site and future changes of use within the same Use Class, in the interests of highway safety and to protect nearby land uses and the character of the area.

Condition : 6 - The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and any subsequent approved revisions.

Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 7 - Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved evidence (schedule of fittings and manufacturers literature) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the development has achieved an internal water use of 105 Litres per person per day or less.

Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.

Condition : 8 - a)	The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of delivery notes, invoices or installation contracts) have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development meets the following:

b)	No building hereby permitted shall be occupied in any given phase until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the approved details under Part (a) of this condition.

The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details at all times thereafter.

Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and in order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.

Condition : 9 - No demolition or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, including the agreed programme and methodology of site evaluation and the competent person(s) or organisation nominated to undertake the agreed works.

If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1, then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI, which shall include:

a)	The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.

b)	Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits.

c)	The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the stage 2 WSI.

Reason: In order to safeguard the special architectural and historic interest of the area.

Condition : 12 - No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until, a Delivery & Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation.

The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved delivery and servicing plan (or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) and shall be maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 13 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which this permission refers, shall be 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, at all times that the plant operate. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance to the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved. 

b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter.   

c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) to which the application refers, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the local planning authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again.  This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard.  Once achieved, the plant shall be maintained permanently ther

Condition : 14 - Prior to commencement of the development, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Council, of the sound insulation of the floor/ ceiling/ walls separating the commercial part(s) of the premises from dwellings. Details shall demonstrate that the sound insulation value DnT,w is enhanced by at least 10dB above the Building Regulations value and, where necessary, additional mitigation measures are implemented to contain commercial noise within the commercial premises and to achieve the criteria of BS8233:2014 within the dwellings/ noise sensitive premises. Approved details shall be implemented prior to occupation of the development and thereafter be permanently retained.

Reason: To ensure that the amenity of occupiers of the development site/ adjacent dwellings/ noise sensitive premises is not adversely affected by noise.

Condition : 15 - Noise mitigation

Prior to the ground floor commercial premises being brought into first use, a Management Plan, including a Noise Management Plan, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved plan.

Reason: In order to safeguard the amenities of the locality.

Condition : 16 - Noise and pollution - sound insulation compliance

Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, post-completion noise assessment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The post completion noise assessment shall comply with the following terms:

i.	The post completion noise assessment shall be carried out by accredited/approved organisations with competence in environmental noise assessments for residential accommodation and take account of worst-case environmental conditions, such as easterly operations at Heathrow Airport, peak time traffic flows, wind speed and direction, presence of temperature inversion and the neighbouring Church premises to the south on Sundays. 

ii.	Where necessary, mitigation measures for the sound insulation and noise reduction of the proposed dwellings against the transmission of the external environmental conditions described in part i (above) shall be implemented, to achieve the criteria of British Standard 8233:2014 within the new dwellings.

iii.	If internal noise levels fail to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again. This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the required standard. The approved details shall be implemented and retained permanently thereafter.

Reason: In order to secure acceptable living conditions for residents of the new dwellings.

Supporting Note:

The maximum noise levels permitted within the dwellings should not exceed those that are specified in Table 4 of British Standard 8233:2014 [Living Rooms = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Dining room/area = 40 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Bedroom = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours during day-time (07:00 - 23:00) and Bedroom = 30 dB LAeq, 8 hours during night-time (23:00 - 07:00)], or any equivalent standards if replaced.

Condition : 17 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details (including manufacturer's specifications) of all cycle stands for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.

Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 18 - No development (above ground, excluding site investigation and clearance) shall take place until a detailed Construction Method Statement (CMS), covering the application site and any adjoining land which will be used during the construction period, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The approved strategy (or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) shall be implemented for the duration of the construction period.

Reason: In order to ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved and to safeguard the amenities of adjoining residential properties.

Condition : 19 - No development above ground level shall take place until full details of the Electric Vehicle Charging Points, each capable of  a minimum output of 7.2kW, are submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include manufacturer's specifications and the number of spaces provided with active and passive capabilities shall comply with the London Plan standards.
The charging points shall be installed in accordance with the approved details, with photographic evidence submitted to the Local Planning Authority upon completion, and so maintained at all times thereafter.
Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Condition : 20 - Blue badge spaces

Prior to the occupation of the hereby approved development the blue badge parking space shown on the approved plans shall be implemented in accordance with the approved plans and shall thereafter be retained as such for the lifetime of the development, without obstruction.

Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Condition : 21 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until full details of the arrangements for the storing of waste and recycled materials (including details of how the placing of waste and recycled materials in a suitable location for collection would be undertaken and managed) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling.

Condition : 22 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:

Following the completion of the Phase I desk study report, if intrusive investigations or gas monitoring is recommended, a Phase II site investigation must be undertaken.

No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.

The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting Notes:

I.	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work.

II.	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.

III.	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local planning authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where it is deeme

Condition : 23 - Prior to commencement of the development hereby approved:

If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting Notes:

I.	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.

II.	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority.

III.	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

IV.	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 24 - During the development:

The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.

A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting notes:

I.	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

II.	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.

III.	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 25 - Prior to the development is first brought into use:

The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting notes:

I.	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement.

II.	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.

III.	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.

Condition : 26 - Land quality - long term monitoring and maintenance

If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the local planning authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice.

This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice.

Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.

Condition : 27 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations and updated Drainage Assessment Form to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the Surface Water Drainage Strategy JE/VL/P23-2848/06 Rev D (June 2023) and associated drawings. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be stated.

Reason: In order to prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.

Condition : 28 - No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.

Reason: In order to ensure that the methods to mitigate the risk of surface water flooding have been implemented as agreed and that the drainage system is suitably managed.

Condition : 29 - Artificial lighting as part of the completed development shall be designed to meet the Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior Lighting Installations for Environmental Zone - E2 set out in Table 2 of the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, 01/21 (https://theilp.org.uk/publication/guidance-note-1-for-the-reduction-of-obtrusive-light-2021/) or such other guidance as may supersede it. The installation shall be examined by a lighting engineer affiliated to a nationally recognised body that specialises in the field of external lighting and certified to confirm that it complies with this standard before it is first brought into use and a copy of the certificate supplied to the local planning authority to confirm compliance before the lights are first brought into operation.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 30 - The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO).

No dwelling shall be occupied until accreditation has been achieved and evidence of such accreditation has been submitted to the local planning authority.

Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.

Condition : 31 - All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development hereby approved shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance (SPG) 'Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' dated July 2014, or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/.

The development shall also demonstrate that the proposed development is complaint with Building Emissions Benchmark (BEBs), specified in the GLA's Supplementary Planning Guidance "Sustainable Design and Construction" dated April 2014).

Reason: To minimise air pollution in the interests of air quality and the wider local environment.

Condition : 32 - Details of any external plant to be installed on the building hereby approved shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement of the development. Such details shall include any necessary sound reduction strategy/mitigation measures. No further fans, louvres, ducts or other external plant shall be installed without the written prior approval of the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the area and neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 33 - Watching Brief

Prior to the commencement of the development, a watching brief for bats shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall commence in accordance with the approved details.

The watching brief shall include:

�	Details of the pre-development check (no more than a week prior to the beginning).

�	Details of the toolbox talk with anyone involved with the construction of development to make them aware of the potential presence of the bats and what to do in event of finding any.

�	Careful working procedures-to be defined in the statement. 

�	Details of who will be watching the construction and what qualifications they hold.

�	A contingency plan of what to do in case of finding a bat roost.

Reason: To ensure the protection of protected species that may be found on the site and in accordance with NPPF.

Condition : 34 - Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, full details of all proposed tree planting and hedgerows shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. This will include planting and maintenance specifications, including cross-section drawings, use of guards or other protective measures and confirmation of location, species and sizes, nursery stock type, supplier, and defect period. Monitoring and management plan of planted trees (and or hedgerows) should be provided (including the work schedule and reporting) to the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.

Condition : 35 - Prior to the occupation of the units hereby approved a scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority providing details of screening to be installed to external amenity areas, including private balconies and the communal garden, to restrict overlooking into neighbouring properties. The proposal shall be implemented in accordance with the approved scheme.

Reason: To prevent overlooking of the nearby premises.

Condition : 36 - Restriction on hours of use

The use of the ground floor commercial premises (Use Class E(a)) hereby permitted shall not be open to customers outside the following times: 06:00am to 23:00pm Mondays to Saturdays and 10:00am to 18:00pm on Sundays and Bank Holidays.

No operations shall take place on Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.

Condition : 37 - Deliveries and collections / loading or unloading shall only occur at the development between the hours of 07:00am to 22:00pm on Mondays to Fridays, 09:00am to 13:00pm on Saturdays, Sundays and Public/Bank Holidays.

Reason: To ensure that the amenity of future occupiers, neighbours and surrounding premises are not adversely affected by noise.
